## TL;DR

Direct task self-checks now compare tracked source working-tree state at check start and end, in addition to comparing HEAD. If tracked source content changes while the check runs, the check fails with the affected paths and does not print “All checks passed.” Bookkeeping paths under `work/` and `.repoos/` are excluded. The focused production-path test suite passed, and `repoos check --changed main` passed with remote validation on bee and all local checks.

## Work and rationale

Review 14 found that a direct task check only compared HEAD at the start and end. That detects a committed source change but misses an uncommitted edit made during the check, because HEAD remains unchanged. The check then could report a green result for a source tree different from the one it started with.

I added a tracked-source snapshot around task self-check execution. The snapshot records Git’s raw tracked diff against HEAD with full object IDs, excludes configured bookkeeping roots, and maps each path to its diff metadata. Comparing per-path metadata identifies exactly which tracked source paths changed during the run, including content and mode changes, without reporting unchanged pre-existing edits as new drift. If either snapshot cannot be obtained, the check fails closed with a clear comparison error. A failed snapshot comparison joins the existing `worktree-drift` failure and prevents reusable check evidence.

The production-path tests run `cmdCheck` in an unmanaged task worktree. One check command changes `src/app.ts` without committing; the test expects exit 1, the source path in the message, and no “All checks passed.” A second command edits the tracked task file under `work/`; it remains bookkeeping-only and the check passes. The fixture also retains coverage for committed source drift during a direct self-check.

The source edit test makes the tracked file writable inside the simulated running check because the existing gate lock changes tracked source file modes while active. This models an already-running process that can bypass that reversible filesystem guard. The owner has explicitly accepted the broader limitation that arbitrary writes by a process already running as an engineer cannot be reliably fenced; post-check drift detection is the safeguard.

## Approaches tried

I used a Git raw diff snapshot rather than HEAD alone, status names alone, or a whole-repository content copy. Raw per-path object IDs let the checker compare tracked source file state precisely while applying Git pathspec exclusions for bookkeeping. The comparison is taken after the gate lock is acquired and before remote validation begins, then repeated after the local check plan and before the lock is released.

The first test attempt exposed that the lock had made the source fixture read-only, so the shell command failed before exercising drift detection. I updated the fixture command to restore owner write permission during the simulated active engineer run, then write the uncommitted edit. The source commit and bookkeeping fixtures exercise the same production command path.

## Challenges and blockers

The key edge case was separating tracked source edits from bookkeeping updates while preserving exact changed-path reporting. Comparing whole snapshots as strings could have blamed an unchanged, pre-existing dirty source path when another path changed. Per-path raw diff metadata avoids that: only paths whose metadata differs between the two snapshots are named.

The isolated preview-request E2E that had failed in an earlier handoff attempt passed locally. During this session, remote validation initially hung on ThinkPad and retried on bee; the changed-path gate then passed there in 701 seconds. Local formatting, lint, build, rendered contrast, UI smoke, and user-docs build also passed.

## Key learnings

HEAD drift and working-tree drift are separate signals. A direct check needs both: commit history explains branch movement, while a tracked worktree snapshot catches uncommitted source edits that leave HEAD untouched. Snapshotting per path yields useful refusal messages and avoids falsely attributing bookkeeping changes.

The merge from `main` is present, and `repoos.toml` matches `main`: `git diff main -- repoos.toml` is empty, and the file is absent from `git diff main...HEAD --name-only`. The accepted commit-then-revert limitation remains documented separately: if source content is identical at the endpoint, the net-tree drift check accepts it. Detecting those intermediate trees is an accepted follow-up, not part of this change.
